# Upstream image conformance corpus

This directory copies the compatible portions of
`/Users/jpo/dev/image/test/_data` so `image_ffmpeg` can exercise the same real
regression corpus without depending on another checkout at test time.

Copied source sets:

| Format | Files |
|---|---:|
| JPEG (including one PNG reference) | 63 |
| PNG / PNGSuite | 198 |
| GIF | 12 |
| WebP (including three PNG references) | 33 |
| TIFF | 26 |
| BMP | 10 |
| ICO | 3 |

The 345 upstream files occupy about 29 MB. PSD was deliberately omitted because
its local corpus is about 79 MB and mostly consists of four large regression
inputs. EXR, PNM, PVR, and TGA were omitted because they are outside the reduced
`image_ffmpeg` API's format allow-list. The small curated format suite under
`../image_formats` still covers PSD and AVIF.

`IMAGE_PACKAGE_LICENSE` is the license copied from the source package. The
PNGSuite license remains beside those fixtures at
`image/png/PngSuite.LICENSE`. Refresh the copied corpus from a sibling checkout
(or pass an explicit checkout path) with:

```bash
tool/update_image_corpus.sh [/path/to/image]
```

## Independent visual references

`references/imagemagick` contains normalized RGBA8888 PNGs generated by
ImageMagick, not by `image_ffmpeg`. They cover:

- all 30 interlaced/non-interlaced PNGSuite baseline images;
- the first frame of all five APNGs.

The exact generator version is recorded in `GENERATOR.txt`. Regenerate them
with:

```bash
tool/update_image_corpus_references.sh
```

The native tests decode these ordinary PNG references and compare
premultiplied RGBA values. On a mismatch they write human-viewable `actual`,
`expected`, and amplified `diff_x8` PNGs under
`native_test/test/failures/image_corpus`.

## Reviewed TIFF regression goldens

`goldens/tiff` contains one viewable PNG for every TIFF that the pinned FFmpeg
build can decode to RGBA. Unlike the PNG/APNG references above, these are
intentionally generated from `image_ffmpeg` itself: they establish a reviewed
visual regression contract rather than declaring another TIFF implementation
normative. The native test compares them exactly.

Regenerate them after an intentional decoder-output change, then visually
review all resulting PNG changes before accepting them:

```bash
cd native_test
dart run bin/update_tiff_goldens.dart
dart test test/image_corpus_reference_test.dart
```

## Intentional known gaps

The suite pins current behavior rather than silently dropping difficult files:

- seven 32/64-bit TIFFs fail during probe.

The newly supported float32 TIFF and all five APNGs have positive decode and
pixel-regression coverage. The four animated WebP regressions using
`ANIM`/`ANMF` are positive first-frame decode tests under the pinned post-8.1
FFmpeg snapshot. All other TIFFs have exact reviewed PNG goldens; no
ImageMagick interpretation is used as their correctness oracle.

The 14 corrupt PNGSuite `x*` images and four historical `broken/` regressions
have bounded no-crash/no-hang tests. FFmpeg is intentionally allowed either to
reject them or to return a geometrically valid image, since parser strictness
varies between versions.
